subtitle: Understanding how verses function as the narrative and harmonic foundation of songs

introduction.title: The Verse: Foundation of Song Narrative
introduction.text: Verses serve as the narrative backbone of songs, providing story development while maintaining harmonic stability. They establish the key center, introduce melodic themes, and create a comfortable foundation for the more dramatic sections that follow.

columns.title: Harmonic Home
columns.text: Establishes and reinforces the tonic key center

columns.title: Story Development
columns.text: Provides lyrical content and narrative progression

columns.title: Musical Balance
columns.text: Creates stability that contrasts with dynamic sections

cards.title: Harmonic Function
cards.description: Usually establishes and reinforces the tonic key

fields.label: Theory
fields.value: Often uses I-vi-IV-V or similar progressions that feel stable

fields.label: Example
fields.value: C-Am-F-G in C major maintains tonal center

fields.label: Theory
fields.value: Stays within an octave, avoids extreme leaps

fields.label: Example
fields.value: Stepwise motion with occasional thirds and fourths

cards.title: Rhythmic Character
cards.description: Steady, predictable patterns that support lyrics

fields.label: Theory
fields.value: Simple subdivision patterns, clear beat emphasis

fields.label: Example
fields.value: Quarter note emphasis in 4/4 with consistent phrasing

fields.label: Example
fields.value: Rhythm guitar, bass, light drums, minimal lead elements

cards.title: I-vi-IV-V (Pop Progression)
items: Extremely stable, feels like "home." The vi chord provides mild contrast while IV-V creates gentle forward motion back to I.

cards.title: ii-V-I (Jazz Influence)
items: Strong sense of resolution. The ii-V motion creates expectation that resolves satisfyingly to I, making verses feel complete.

cards.title: Musical Elements
items: Key center: What key is established?
Chord progression: What functional harmony is used?
Melodic range: How wide is the vocal melody?
Rhythm: What subdivision and feel?
Texture: How dense is the arrangement?

cards.title: Structural Elements
items: Form: AABA, ABAB, or through-composed?
Length: How many measures per verse?
Repetition: What elements repeat vs. develop?
Contrast: How does it differ from chorus?
Connection: How does it lead to the next section?

practiceSection.title: Practice Exercises
items: Listening Analysis: Choose a song and isolate just the verse sections
Listening Analysis: Identify the chord progression by ear
Listening Analysis: Notice the melodic range and contour
Listening Analysis: Count measures and identify the formal structure
Listening Analysis: Compare multiple verses—what stays the same vs. what changes?
Playing Practice: Learn verse chord progressions from different genres
Playing Practice: Practice transitioning from verse to chorus smoothly
Playing Practice: Experiment with different strumming patterns for verses
Playing Practice: Try playing verse progressions in different keys
Playing Practice: Write your own verse using common progressions
